Node.brief: Base class for everything that lives in a scene tree.
Node.description: Node is the base class for everything in a Corbel scene tree. A node has a name, an optional parent, children, an owner, and groups. The tree calls lifecycle methods in order: _enter_tree when the node joins the live tree, _ready after the children are ready (children run before the parent, like Godot), _process once per frame, _input on every event that the runner feeds the tree, and _exit_tree when the node leaves. queue_free removes the node at the end of the frame. Scripts get these hooks by overriding them with the same names in TypeScript: a class extends Node (or a subclass) and overrides _ready(). Throw nothing you cannot survive: a throw inside _ready or _process is reported through SceneTree.on_node_error and the frame keeps running.

Node3D.brief: Base for nodes with a place in 3D space: position, rotation, basis, visibility.
Node3D.description: Node3D adds a place in 3D space. rotation is stored as a Basis and written back through rotation (radians) or rotation_degrees. transform composes both into a Transform3D. Every subclass that draws or moves inherits this class. The world is Y-up and right-handed; a camera looks down local -Z, so a node authored to face the camera points its +Z at it.

properties.name: rotation
properties.desc: Euler radians. Setting it replaces the basis

properties.name: basis
properties.desc: The rotation, stored as a Basis

properties.name: transform
properties.desc: Basis plus position as a Transform3D

Camera3D.brief: The view the renderer draws through.
Camera3D.description: Camera3D is the view. fov is vertical degrees, 75 like Godot. near and far clip it. current picks the camera: the last current camera in tree order draws, or the first camera when none is current. The camera looks down its local -Z.

properties.name: fov
properties.desc: Vertical field of view in degrees. Default 75, like Godot

properties.name: current
properties.desc: Marks this camera as the one the renderer draws through

GeometryInstance3D.brief: Base class for nodes a renderer can draw.
GeometryInstance3D.description: GeometryInstance3D is the base every draw node inherits from in Godot. In the foundation, MeshInstance3D is its only concrete subclass today.

MeshInstance3D.brief: A node that draws the mesh assigned to its geometry.
MeshInstance3D.description: MeshInstance3D draws its geometry when it holds a Mesh, and material_override carries the color or texture. It can be added, moved, hidden, and saved. The weave attaches project scripts to scene nodes by their script_path meta, so a saved MeshInstance3D can carry a .ts script.

properties.name: geometry
properties.desc: The mesh to draw. Nothing draws while it is null

properties.name: material_override
properties.desc: The material the surface draws with. StandardMaterial3D or ShaderMaterial

DirectionalLight3D.brief: A sun-style light that shines along the node's local -Z.
DirectionalLight3D.description: DirectionalLight3D shines along the node's local -Z, so an unrotated light points (0, 0, -1). The first DirectionalLight3D in tree order lights the scene. Rotate the node to aim the light, exactly like Godot's sun.

properties.name: light_color
properties.desc: The light's color. White by default

WorldEnvironment.brief: Overrides the tree's background and ambient look.
WorldEnvironment.description: WorldEnvironment is a node that overrides the tree's look: assign it an Environment with background_color (what the canvas clears to) and ambient. The renderer picks the first WorldEnvironment in the tree; none means the default dark background and dim ambient.

properties.name: environment
properties.desc: The Environment with background_color and ambient

Environment.brief: Resource holding the tree's background and ambient.
Environment.description: Environment holds the tree's look data: background_color is what the canvas clears to, ambient is the ambient light color that lighting adds to every surface. WorldEnvironment carries this resource.

Timer.brief: A node that counts a wait_time and emits timeout.
Timer.description: Timer counts a wait_time every frame it is allowed to run and emits timeout when it crosses zero. start(time) begins counting, one_shot stops after a single timeout instead of repeating, autostart calls start on _ready. Pause behaves like Godot: a PAUSABLE Timer waits while the tree is paused and an ALWAYS Timer keeps counting.

properties.name: wait_time
properties.desc: Seconds between the start and timeout

methods.name: start
methods.desc: Begin counting, restarting from the top

methods.name: stop
methods.desc: Stop counting and clear the remainder

methods.name: is_stopped
methods.desc: True while it is not counting

methods.name: get_time_left
methods.desc: Seconds left until timeout. Negative while stopped

methods.name: timeout
methods.desc: Emitted when the wait_time crosses zero

SceneTree.brief: Owns the hidden root, the frame loop, timers, and scene change.
SceneTree.description: new SceneTree() makes a hidden root named root. Add the scene's top node with get_root().add_child(scene). Call _process(delta) once per frame. init({ canvas, preference }) picks a renderer and starts the frame loop: _process in tree order, then a draw. timer support is built in, and change_scene swaps the current level at the end of the frame.

properties.name: paused
properties.desc: Skip _process while it is true; the draw still happens

properties.name: on_node_error
properties.desc: Set a callback to receive _ready and _process errors with the node

properties.name: current_scene
properties.desc: The scene the runner registered, or the latest change_scene node

methods.name: get_root
methods.desc: The hidden root

methods.name: get_nodes_in_group
methods.desc: Every node that joined that group

methods.name: tick
methods.desc: One frame. Parent first, then children, then queued frees, then tree timers

methods.name: init
methods.desc: Pick the renderer and start the frame loop

methods.name: create_timer
methods.desc: An awaitable timer independent of the tree: await timer.timeout. process_always keeps it running while paused (default true)

methods.name: change_scene_to_file
methods.desc: Load the .cscene at the path, weave it, and swap. Returns true on success

methods.name: change_scene_to_packed
methods.desc: Instantiate the PackedScene and swap. The old scene frees at the end of the frame; autoloads survive

methods.name: change_scene_to_node
methods.desc: Swap to a node you already built

methods.name: get_current_scene
methods.desc: The current scene node, or null

methods.name: push_input
methods.desc: Dispatch one event to every node that overrides _input

methods.name: close
methods.desc: Stop the loop and release the renderer

SceneTreeTimer.brief: Created by SceneTree.create_timer; count down and emit timeout.
SceneTreeTimer.description: SceneTreeTimer counts down every frame it is allowed to run, then emits timeout. process_always (true by default) keeps it counting while the tree is paused. awaiting the timeout signal is the Godot idiom:

properties.name: process_always
properties.desc: True it keeps counting while the tree is paused

methods.name: timeout
methods.desc: Emitted when the wait crosses zero

Signal.brief: A list of callbacks, connectable and awaitable.
Signal.description: A Signal is a list of callbacks. connect adds one, disconnect removes it, is_connected checks, emit calls them in connection order. Awaiting a Signal resolves on the next emit, which is how GDScript's await ports:

methods.name: connect
methods.desc: Adds one

methods.name: disconnect
methods.desc: Removes it

methods.name: is_connected
methods.desc: True when it is in the list

methods.name: emit
methods.desc: Calls them in the order they were connected

methods.name: once
methods.desc: A promise that resolves with the emit arguments on the next emit

PackedScene.brief: Saved scene data that instantiate turns into a fresh tree.
PackedScene.description: PackedScene holds saved scene data. instantiate builds a fresh tree each call; from_node packs a live tree; from_data wraps parsed .cscene JSON. Scene files save to .cscene and load back with load("res://level2.cscene") through the ResourceLoader.

methods.name: instantiate
methods.desc: Builds a new tree; the loaded scene weaves project scripts

methods.name: from_node
methods.desc: Packs a live node tree

methods.name: from_data
methods.desc: Wraps parsed .cscene JSON

methods.name: get_name
methods.desc: The scene root's name

ResourceLoader.brief: Loads project resources by path: scenes, textures, scripts, materials.
ResourceLoader.description: The shared ResourceLoader resolves res:// paths by extension and caches by path. Built-in: .cscene loads as a PackedScene. Runtime-registered: .ts loads as the script class, .png/.jpg/.jpeg/.webp/.gif as a Texture2D, .cmaterial as a StandardMaterial3D with its texture loaded. New extensions register with set_loader(ext, handler).

methods.name: load
methods.desc: The cached resource, resolved by extension. Godot's load()

methods.name: set_loader
methods.desc: Register or replace the loader for one extension

methods.name: set_file_loader
methods.desc: The read the loader uses for text files. The runtime wires this

methods.name: has_cached
methods.desc: True when the path already sits in the cache

Input.brief: Action and raw key/button state, fed by parse_input_event.
Input.description: The Input singleton reads the current state every frame. parse_input_event feeds one event: state updates and the tree calls _input. is_action_just_pressed and is_action_just_released hold for one frame; SceneTree.tick advances the frame.

methods.name: is_action_pressed
methods.desc: True while the action is held, device bind or action event

methods.name: is_action_just_pressed
methods.desc: True for the one frame it went down

methods.name: is_action_just_released
methods.desc: True for the one frame it came up

methods.name: is_key_pressed
methods.desc: Raw physical key state, with Godot Key values

methods.name: is_mouse_button_pressed
methods.desc: MouseButton.LEFT and friends

methods.name: get_mouse_position
methods.desc: Canvas pixels

methods.name: parse_input_event
methods.desc: Feed one event: state updates and _input dispatch

InputMap.brief: Named actions bound to events, loaded from the project settings.
InputMap.description: Godot 4 InputMap: actions map to input events. load_from_project installs every action from a parsed settings block. The editor edits them under Project → Project settings… Events match by kind: a physical bind matches the key's position, a layout bind matches what the current keyboard layout produces.

methods.name: add_action
methods.desc: Start an action. Adding an existing name is a no-op, like Godot

methods.name: has_action
methods.desc: True when the action exists

methods.name: get_actions
methods.desc: Every action name

methods.name: erase_action
methods.desc: Delete the action

methods.name: action_add_event
methods.desc: Bind one event to an action

methods.name: action_get_events
methods.desc: A copy of the action's binds

methods.name: action_erase_events
methods.desc: Unbind every event

methods.name: action_get_deadzone
methods.desc: The analog threshold stored with the action; keys ignore it

methods.name: event_is_action
methods.desc: True when the event matches a bind

methods.name: load_from_project
methods.desc: Replace every action from a settings block

ProjectSettings.brief: The parsed project.corbel.json of the running game.
ProjectSettings.description: ProjectSettings.load(data) holds the parsed project settings. Loading installs the Input Map and clears Input state. get(name) reads a top-level key such as window, main_scene, or autoload.

methods.name: load
methods.desc: Parse a settings object; input installs the map

methods.name: get
methods.desc: A top-level key value

methods.name: get_string
methods.desc: A top-level string value, or the fallback

methods.name: has
methods.desc: True when the key was in the file

Resource.brief: Base class for reusable data: materials, meshes, textures, scenes.
Resource.description: Resource is the base of everything loaded or authored as data: Material, Mesh, PackedScene, Texture2D, Environment, and SurfaceTool output. Resources cache by path in the ResourceLoader.

Material.brief: Base class for the way a surface draws.
Material.description: Material is the base class of StandardMaterial3D and ShaderMaterial. A renderer reads the concrete type per draw. Set a material on a MeshInstance3D with material_override.

StandardMaterial3D.brief: The built-in lit material: albedo, texture, roughness, metallic.
StandardMaterial3D.description: StandardMaterial3D draws with the built-in lit shader on both backends. The albedo texture multiplies the albedo color, so a white material shows texture colors; a texture-less material samples a white 1x1 and the albedo color behaves exactly like the pre-texture engine.

properties.name: albedo
properties.desc: The base color. Multiplied by albedo_texture

properties.name: roughness
properties.desc: Present for Godot compatibility; the foundation's lit shader ignores it today

properties.name: metallic
properties.desc: Present for Godot compatibility; the foundation's lit shader ignores it today

properties.name: albedo_texture
properties.desc: The color texture to sample once per UV square

ShaderMaterial.brief: A Shader plus values for its named uniform parameters.
ShaderMaterial.description: ShaderMaterial pairs a Shader with values for the shader's named uniforms. Values arrive at the GPU in the Shader's own parameter order; the WGSL params are vec4, so colors, vectors, and scalars all coerce.

properties.name: shader
properties.desc: The program pair this material draws with

methods.name: set_shader_parameter
methods.desc: Store a uniform value

methods.name: get_shader_parameter
methods.desc: The stored value, or null

methods.name: get_shader_parameter_list
methods.desc: A copy of the values, keyed by name

Shader.brief: One program pair: a WGSL body for WebGPU and a GLSL body for WebGL2.
Shader.description: Shader.lit({ uniforms, webgpu_body, webgl_body }) builds one program pair. The uniforms are vec4 (colors, vectors, and scalars coerce). Both bodies see the same names: color, normal, albedo, light_dir, light_color, ambient, each parameter by its own name, and lighting(normal) (WGSL) or lighting() (GLSL). The body returns the final color.

properties.name: params
properties.desc: Parameter names in the order the uniform buffer carries them

methods.name: lit
methods.desc: Build the program pair from uniform names and the two bodies

Mesh.description: Mesh is the base every renderer-visible geometry inherits: ArrayMesh and BoxMesh today, with the SurfaceTool able to build any of them in code.

ArrayMesh.brief: A mesh built from raw arrays: positions, normals, colors, uvs, indices.
ArrayMesh.description: ArrayMesh wraps one surface of arrays. Use SurfaceTool with PrimitiveType.TRIANGLES to build them one vertex at a time, or write the arrays directly. Triangles wind counter-clockwise seen from outside.

properties.name: arrays
properties.desc: The positions, normals, colors, uvs, tangents, and indices

BoxMesh.brief: A cube centered on the origin.
BoxMesh.description: BoxMesh builds a 24-vertex, 36-index cube with outward normals, white vertex colors, and one 0-1 UV square per face. size controls the extent along each axis.

properties.name: size
properties.desc: The extent along each axis. 1x1x1 by default

Texture2D.brief: A decoded project image the renderer uploads and binds.
Texture2D.description: Texture2D is a decoded project image (PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP). load("res://textures/wall.png") reads it, decodes it, and caches it by path. StandardMaterial3D.albedo_texture multiplies the albedo color; a texture-less material samples a white 1x1, so colors stay exact.

SurfaceTool.brief: Builds a mesh one vertex at a time, the way Godot's SurfaceTool does.
SurfaceTool.description: SurfaceTool builds a mesh with triangles, vertices, normals, colors, UVs, and tangents, and commit hands back an ArrayMesh. begin(PrimitiveType.TRIANGLES), set per-vertex attributes, add_vertex to close each one. Pending attributes reset after every vertex. commit returns an ArrayMesh.

methods.name: set_uv

methods.name: set_color
methods.desc: The next vertex's vertex color

methods.name: set_tangent
methods.desc: Tangent direction, binormal sign in plane.d

methods.name: add_vertex
methods.desc: Closes the pending vertex. Attributes reset after it

methods.name: index
methods.desc: Merge identical vertices and share them by index

methods.name: generate_normals
methods.desc: Smooth each triangle face normal onto its vertices

methods.name: generate_tangents
methods.desc: Fill the tangent from UVs; every vertex needs a UV

methods.name: clear
methods.desc: Start over

methods.name: commit

PrimitiveType.description: POINT, LINES, LINE_STRIP, TRIANGLES, TRIANGLE_STRIP. The renderer draws TRIANGLES surfaces only right now.

Color.description: Godot 4 Color. html("#rrggbb") and to_html() go between web colors and components. r, g, b, a are plain 0-1 numbers.

Plane.description: Godot 4 Plane. distance_to is normal.dot(point) - d, and intersects_ray walks a ray onto the plane (returns null when the ray points away).

InputEvent.brief: Base for input events passed to Node._input.
InputEvent.description: InputEvent base: subclasses carry modifiers. shift_pressed, ctrl_pressed, alt_pressed, and meta_pressed are true, false, or null (this event does not say; binds treat null as any).

properties.name: shift_pressed
properties.desc: Modifier state, or null when the event does not say

methods.name: is_pressed
methods.desc: True when the event is a press

InputEventKey.description: A keyboard event with both codes: key_code is the layout-dependent code, physical_key_code is the position on the US QWERTY keyboard. A bind stores which kind it means; the code flag decides the matching.

properties.name: physical_key_code
properties.desc: Position on the US QWERTY keyboard

properties.name: physical
properties.desc: Which kind this bind stores against, for binds

methods.desc: True for auto-repeat. Actions usually ignore it

InputEventMouseButton.brief: A click from a mouse button.
InputEventMouseButton.description: A click. button_index is one of MouseButton.LEFT, RIGHT, MIDDLE, WHEEL_UP, WHEEL_DOWN. position is in canvas pixels from the top-left.

InputEventMouseMotion.description: Pointer movement: position is the current spot, relative is the movement since the previous motion event. is_pressed is always false.

InputEventAction.brief: A named action event, sent by code.
InputEventAction.description: The InputEventAction.new() equivalent: action, pressed, strength. parse_input_event drives it without any device event.

Key.brief: Godot 4 Key constants: Key.W, Key.SPACE, Key.ESCAPE.
Key.description: Godot 4 @GlobalScope.Key values: letters and digits are ASCII uppercase (Key.W is 87), specials start at Key.SPECIAL = 4194304, so Key.ESCAPE is 4194305 and Key.LEFT is 4194319. F1 through F12 continue from there.

MouseButton.description: Mouse buttons: LEFT = 1, RIGHT = 2, MIDDLE = 3, WHEEL_UP = 4, WHEEL_DOWN = 5.

SurfaceArrays.brief: The arrays one mesh surface carries.
SurfaceArrays.description: The arrays one surface hands to the renderer: positions, optional normals, colors, uvs, tangents (four floats: xyz plus the binormal sign), and indices. Triangles wind counter-clockwise seen from outside. Missing arrays fall back (white colors, +Z normals) so script-built meshes still render.
